methodologyNotes: Ten current high-search gaming headsets spanning budget to flagship tiers (2022-2024 release years), independently re-verified against official manufacturer product pages and newsroom press releases (SteelSeries/GN, Razer, HyperX/HP, Logitech G, Corsair) plus reputable reviews (Tom's Hardware, TechRadar, SoundGuys, PC Gamer, RTINGS). Driver sizes in mm, weights in grams. battery_hours = manufacturer headline wireless figure (RGB off where two figures exist; null for wired). surround_sound and rgb are presence booleans. Adversarial fact-check (2026-06-15) corrected two values: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 priceUsd 149->179.99 (draft's $149/$199 narrative was fabricated; $199 is the Gen 2 price, $179.99 is the original launch MSRP) and Corsair HS80 Max weight_g 352->360 (official Corsair spec page lists 0.36 kg). All ten products verified to exist; all source URLs resolve and are topical. accessedAt 2026-06-15.

products.name: Audeze Maxwell
products.priceNote: Official Audeze product page (audeze.com/products/maxwell) lists price "$299.00 - $329.00" and the comparison table "$299 - $329 USD / Playstation / Xbox version" ($299 PlayStation version; $329 Xbox version, which adds an embedded Dolby Atmos license). Using $299 base MSRP. Page states the original Maxwell "is a legacy product and no longer available for sale."
products.provenance: Fetched the official Audeze Maxwell product page (audeze.com/products/maxwell) via fetch-clean.mjs; its Specifications table confirms verbatim: 90 mm planar-magnetic transducer, Weight 490g, detachable hypercardioid boom microphone, Connection "Wireless" (ultra-low-latency + Bluetooth 5.3), Battery life "Over 80 hrs wireless playback @ 80dBA", and Spatial Audio "Dolby Atmos (Xbox Version) / Tempest 3D (PlayStation Version)" — so surround sound=true and battery hours=80. The page also lists price "$299.00 - $329.00" and marks the original Maxwell as a legacy product. No lighting/RGB appears anywhere in the spec table or marketing, so rgb=false per the catalog's presence-boolean convention; no release date/year is stated on the page, so release and release date are left blank. Adversarial re-fetch (2026-07-08) confirmed the exact model (Maxwell, SKU 208-MW-1120-01, legacy — not Maxwell 2) and every recorded spec verbatim. Retailer corroboration was attempted (Best Buy, B&H Photo, Crutchfield, Newegg, Amazon) but every retailer either aborted the connection, returned HTTP 403, or 404'd, so corroboration is left blank.

The Amazon retail listing (ASIN B09TRW57WB, Model Number 4P5D4AA, Manufacturer HP Inc.) corroborates this exact model at retail: item weight "322 Grams", 300-hour battery, DTS Headphone:X spatial audio, 50mm Dual Chamber drivers, detachable noise-cancelling mic, durable aluminum frame, wireless 2.4GHz. Not a sibling (Cloud Alpha 2 / Alpha S / Cloud III are listed as separate products). No RGB lighting (the mic has only a red mute-status LED); rgb=false per catalog convention for non-RGB models. All 8 spec keys, the price, and release date survive verification.

No RGB or lighting is mentioned on either comprehensive spec page (rgb false), and neither fetched page states a release date, so release date and release are left blank.

No. 730084-B, EAN 4010118730085) is the exact MMX 200 wireless model; its technical-data table confirms: Transmission Type Wireless via Bluetooth 5.3, 40 mm driver systems, weight without cable 360 g, battery runtime up to 35 hours, detachable META VOICE microphone (9.9 mm capsule, cardioid electret condenser), 32 ohms, 20 Hz-20,000 Hz, closed over-ear.
